subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should OpenClaw status/doctor memory health be sourced from the live gateway runtime, a passive plugin status API, or the existing local status-manager path?
rationale: Current main only changes wording, while the linked fork PR is a narrow provider fallback and the adjacent open issue shows the local status-manager path can run plugin startup side effects.

options.title: Adopt live-runtime health
options.body: Replace or repair the linked PR with a doctor/status payload that separates runtime health from embedding readiness and uses the live gateway as the source of truth when available.

options.title: Require passive plugin status
options.body: Keep local plugin status reporting only if memory plugins get a no-side-effect passive status contract and regression coverage for third-party plugins.

options.title: Keep current mitigation
options.body: Leave `not checked` as the status wording and close the fork PR, accepting that live memory health is not reported by status for these plugins.

recommendation.title: Adopt live-runtime health
recommendation.body: Replace or repair the linked PR with a doctor/status payload that separates runtime health from embedding readiness and uses the live gateway as the source of truth when available.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to both the memory-runtime plugin-routing refactor and the custom memory status mitigation that shape the remaining product boundary.
